To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in a child with chronic hepatitis, we have found intranuclear hepatitis viruslike particles and in a portal tract of the liver, virus budding in a mononuclear cell.

in the present study we have found in the liver biopsied from a child with chronic NANB hepatitis: (1) viruslike core particles in the nucleus and (2) viruslike budding particles in the mononuclear cells of the inflammatory infiltrate.

in the course of a study of 16 cases of NANB, we found a case with HBsAg and HBeAg seronegativity in which the liver biopsy contained intranuclear hepatitis virus-like particles and a case in which the biopsy contained viruslike particles with a retrovirus-like appearance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for viruses in the liver of patients with NANB hepatitis.
the possibility of the presence of a virus with a morphology similar to that of retrovirus in the liver of a child suffering from chronic NANB hepatitis.
the study of the ultrastructural features of the liver in children with NANB hepatitis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the virus-like particles we have observed in the liver biopsied of two patients with NANB hepatitis could be either HBV-like or retrovirus-like.
these observations are suggestive of the presence of a retrovirus in the liver biopsied from the child with chronic NANB hepatitis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have observed in the liver biopsys of children with chronic NANB hepatitis: 1) viruslike particles in the cytoplasm and in the nucleus of hepatocytes; 2) viruslike particles budding from mononuclear cells; 3) a high frequency of lymphocytes with surface membrane receptors for IgG and IgM, but not for IgA.
we have observed, for the first time, viruslike structures that could represent a NANB virus in the cytoplasm of hepatocytes and in the cytoplasma of mononuclear cells.
we have found in one case of chronic NANB hepatitis, intranuclear corelike particles that resemble HBV, and in another, budding particles that resemble retrovirus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the viruslike particles described in the two cases are not identical.
we have observed, in one biopsy, the presence of both hepatitis B virus and retrovirus-like particles.
the viruslike particles described above could be a new type of virus, different from the known hepatitis viruses.
